title: Artistic Full Hand Sunburst Mehndi Design for Front Hand
descriptionParagraphs: An elegant full hand mehndi design tailored for the palm, featuring paisley and anklet border. Rated as Medium, this pattern is perfect for an engagement.

The palm has the thickest skin on the hand, so henna stains darkest here. Keep the hand open and relaxed while the paste dries so the lines do not crack or smudge. This pattern suits someone who is already comfortable with basic lines, dots and petals and wants to practise even spacing.
Full-hand mehndi covers the hand from the fingertips to the wrist and often continues up the forearm. It is the usual choice for brides and for major festivals where a heavier look is wanted.

Application tips: Dab a lemon and sugar mixture on the dried paste to keep it moist and stuck to the skin. Scrape the dried paste off instead of washing it, and keep the area away from water for the first 12 to 24 hours.

image.alt: Full Hand Sunburst mehndi design for front hand — artistic henna pattern

faq.q: Should both hands have the same full-hand design?
faq.a: They can match, mirror each other, or use two related designs. Mirrored designs are the most traditional.

faq.q: How long does a mehndi stain last?
faq.a: A natural henna stain usually lasts one to three weeks. It fades faster on areas that are washed or rubbed often, such as the hands.

faq.q: How long should I leave the mehndi paste on?
faq.a: Keep the paste on for at least four to six hours. Many people leave it overnight for a darker stain.

title: Bold Full Hand Net Pattern Mehndi Design for Arm
descriptionParagraphs: A traditional full hand mehndi design tailored for the arm, featuring ring pattern and chain link. Rated as Medium, this pattern is perfect for everyday.

Henna on the forearm stains lighter than on the palm because the skin is thinner. Arm designs are easier to apply on someone else than on yourself, especially past the wrist. This pattern suits someone who is already comfortable with basic lines, dots and petals and wants to practise even spacing.
A detailed full-hand design can take an hour or more per hand. Full-hand layouts usually combine several motifs, such as a mandala, a jaal (net) and paisleys, in separate sections.
Application tips: The stain starts orange and darkens to reddish brown over 24 to 48 hours as it oxidises. Wash and dry the skin before application and skip lotion or oil, which block the dye.
